title: Batch Prompting
summary: Amortize work across independent items while preserving item identity, isolation, validation, and retry boundaries.
overview: Batch prompting places several logically separate items into one model request and asks for an item-indexed response. It can amortize repeated instructions for small homogeneous tasks, but it shares context and failure fate across the items. A malformed response, truncated output, or adversarial item can affect the whole batch.

This differs from server-side inference batching, where an engine schedules independent requests together, and from asynchronous batch APIs, which submit many independent requests for deferred processing. Those mechanisms need not combine user data into one prompt. Architects should choose the appropriate batching layer before accepting the isolation and reliability costs of prompt-level packing.

production.poc: A prototype compares one-item calls with small homogeneous prompt batches and checks item-level accuracy.
production.production: Production assigns stable item IDs, caps input and output budgets, and validates that every expected item appears exactly once.
production.scale: At scale, separate tenant and policy scopes, use adaptive batch sizing, and retry only failed items while monitoring head-of-line delay and cross-item contamination.

components.name: Batch builder
components.role: Groups compatible items under shared task, policy, and deadline constraints.

components.name: Prompt envelope
components.role: Separates item data and specifies an item-indexed output schema.

components.name: Token estimator
components.role: Bounds total input and expected output before dispatch.

components.name: Result demultiplexer
components.role: Maps model outputs back to stable item IDs and detects omissions or duplicates.

components.name: Retry queue
components.role: Resubmits failed items independently without repeating accepted results.

flow.title: Choose the batching layer
flow.description: Decide whether prompt packing, engine batching, or deferred independent requests fit the workload.

flow.title: Group compatible items
flow.description: Require the same task contract and permitted data-sharing scope.

flow.title: Assign identities and budget
flow.description: Give every item a stable ID and reserve sufficient output capacity.

flow.title: Execute the batch
flow.description: Submit the bounded prompt and retain the batch-to-item mapping.

flow.title: Validate each result
flow.description: Check schema, coverage, duplicate IDs, and task acceptance per item.

flow.title: Retry selectively
flow.description: Split or resubmit only missing or failed items with preserved identity.

useCase.title: Tagging a catalog of short descriptions
useCase.situation: A media team classifies thousands of short program descriptions into a stable editorial taxonomy.
useCase.problem: Single-item requests repeat long instructions, while oversized batches omit items near the end.
useCase.requirement: Reduce repeated prompt overhead without losing item-level accountability.
useCase.architecture: The batch builder groups similar short descriptions and requires one structured result per catalog ID.
runtime: A bounded group is sent with a fixed taxonomy and explicit IDs.
The demultiplexer accepts valid tags and retries only omitted descriptions.
useCase.failure: If one item contains instruction-like text, it remains data and cannot alter the batch taxonomy; contaminated results are rejected.
useCase.impact: Measure cost per accepted item, omission rate, batch latency, and contamination; aggregate response success does not mean every catalog record was processed.

tradeoffs.cost: May have different latency and service limits.

failures.detection: Expected and returned item sets differ.
failures.recovery: Retry missing items in smaller groups.

failures.detection: Cross-item leakage appears in labeled evaluation.
failures.recovery: Separate prompts or use independent request batching.

mistakes.fix: Distinguish prompt, engine, and asynchronous API layers.
Enforce a common authorized data scope.
Track and retry only unsuccessful items.

whenToUse: Use for small homogeneous classification or extraction items.
Use when shared instructions dominate request cost.
Use when per-item validation is reliable.
whenNotToUse: Avoid prompt packing across incompatible privacy scopes.
Avoid large variable-length outputs with unpredictable budgets.
Do not use it for items requiring independent conversational reasoning.
